text: Is the voice on the phone actually that of her father’s daughter?
Is the "kidnapping" staged, in the sense that no real hostage is in danger?
Is the daughter herself involved in carrying out the kidnapping scheme?
Does the father refuse to pay because he believes paying would harm or endanger his daughter?
Does the father believe the kidnapper will kill the daughter regardless of whether the ransom is paid?
Does the father suspect that the "kidnapper" is someone known to the family, such as a relative?
Does the father believe that the kidnapper is capable of killing the daughter if the demand is not met?
Does the father believe the "kidnapper" is not a genuine threat—for example, that the caller is not actually holding his daughter?
Does the father have reason to believe that paying the ransom would lead the kidnapper to kill the daughter anyway, contrary to what the kidnapper claims?
Does the father know or suspect that the 100 million yen itself would enable the kidnapper to harm the daughter or is otherwise tied to a lethal trap?
Does the father refuse to pay because he recognizes the demand as a known type of scam or extortion in which victims who pay are still killed or never released?
Does the father believe the daughter can be saved without paying, for example by police or by rescue after he alerts authorities?

Does the father believe the caller's claim that the daughter is held hostage is false in a specific way—for instance, that the person speaking as his daughter is not a hostage but is being coerced to make the call?
